description: Claude Desktop by its MSIX family name, Cursor and Windsurf by their Uninstall keys, Cursor running and Claude's browser bridge registered.
why: The two Windows-only routes against real installs, beside a portable one. Claude Desktop's identity is its package family name, not its display name; Cursor's and Windsurf's are the Uninstall keys their installers choose, and the DisplayName in `extra` is what tells a reader which is which. The bridge is the value macOS already carries, reached here through the registry. `forbid` keeps Claude Desktop's rows from being read as Claude Code or the Claude extension, and the editors' rows from being read as an editor extension.
known_gaps: Each per-user install is read while its user is signed in: HKEY_USERS holds loaded hives only, so the same install by a user who is signed out leaves no Uninstall or MSIX row (docs/blind-spots.yaml).
Windsurf is not launched, so its liveness is unproven.
Claude Desktop wrote its browser bridge only once a Chrome profile existed, so the nmh row is proof for a machine with Chrome set up; one without reads Claude Desktop through its MSIX row alone.
Sign-in gated, as on macOS: nothing exercises behaviour that appears once a user signs in.
